context: Found during the corpus rule PR's preflight on 2026-11-26. Failing log kept at ~/.cache/benchbox/crr/preflight-821-attempt1.log (local).
description:
## Problem
tests/unit/core/test_partial_generation_data.py::test_a_directory_left_by_a_killed_generator_is_regenerated[tpcds] failed once in a serial `make pr-preflight` on a loaded host (2026-11-26, corpus rule branch head 8218cfa86b): `FileNotFoundError: .../data/store_sales.dat` at the partial-file assertion (line 106 at that head). The same test passed in the preflight one commit earlier, and that branch does not touch the test or the generator code. The test came with #4434.

The `deadline` fixture freezes the deadline clock so that only a short real-time window remains (0.3 s: a 1 s deadline with the fake clock advanced 0.7 s; the stub is a separate Python process that must start and write within it), then expects the stub generator to have written a partial `store_sales.dat` before the run deadline kills it. When the host is busy, the kill can arrive before the stub writes anything, so the test races real time.

## Change
- Make the ordering explicit: the kill must happen only after the stub has written its partial file. The deadline turns its fake remaining time into a real wait when it arms the kill (`threading.Timer(self.remaining(), ...)` in `RunDeadline.stream`, `communicate(timeout=self.remaining())` in `RunDeadline.run`, benchbox/utils/run_deadline.py), so advancing the fake clock after arming has no effect. Have the stub signal once it has written (for example a ready file) and fire the kill from the test only after that signal, using test seams only (for example a timer the test controls).
- Keep what the test proves: a directory left by a killed generator carries the in-progress marker, no manifest and a short file, and the next run regenerates it.

## Decision gates
- If determinism needs a change to product code (benchbox/utils/run_deadline.py or a generator), stop and report the scope before changing it.
- Raising the real-time window or adding a retry is not a fix.

## Verification rubric
- A forced reproduction (the stub sleeps before writing) fails before the fix and passes after.
- The TPC-H and TPC-DS cases both pass when repeated at least 20 times in one serial session under make heavy-run.

## Guardrails
- Reproduce or measure before changing anything; record the command, log path and run id in the item context.
- Fix the root cause. Never skip, xfail, loosen a check or bound, or raise a timeout only to make a test or run pass; a timing or limit change needs measured evidence and owner approval.
- No rule, check, label or test may name a platform or a version matrix unless the item is about that platform.
- Never edit stored result files under results-data/ or CHANGELOG.md; user-facing changes add a changelog.d fragment.
- No explanatory comments or docstrings (make comment-policy-check); make duplicate-check-delta stays at +0; reuse existing helpers.
- Heavy work only through make heavy-run after make heavy-status, with command, maximum run time and log path announced first. Never touch the lock or set BENCHBOX_SKIP_TEST_LOCK, BENCHBOX_HEAVY_ADMIT=force, BENCHBOX_HEAVY_WATCHDOG=off, or raise BENCHBOX_HEAVY_MEMORY_BUDGET_GIB. No live cloud runs.
- Work in a linked worktree; one pull request; run the local review before opening it; fix hosted-review findings. No stand-in approval unless the owner names the PR and head.
- Re-read paths and line numbers before editing and report drift instead of guessing.
- When a decision gate's stop condition is met, stop and report to the owner with the evidence; never substitute a different decision.
